title: [critic] prop:status(III) orthogonality ⟨ξ,η⟩=0 inferred from first-moment E[QBQ^T]=0 — invalid inference

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** `solution.tex`, Proposition `prop:status`, item (III), and Remark `rem:honest`.

The MSS/Stam-reduction route requires hypothesis (iii) of Lemma `lem:reduction`, namely $\langle\xi,\eta\rangle_H=0$ where $H=L^2(O(n),\mu;\mathbb R^n)$ and $\langle u,v\rangle_H=\mathbb E_Q\langle u(Q),v(Q)\rangle$.

**The claimed justification is invalid.** The text asserts (III) holds because "the off-block first moment $\mathbb E_Q(QBQ^\top)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}B}{n}I$ vanishes after centring ($\operatorname{tr}B=0$), which is the finite-$n$ form of asymptotic freeness." Two problems:

1. $\langle\xi,\eta\rangle_H=\mathbb E_Q\langle\xi(Q),\eta(Q)\rangle$ is the average of an inner product of two (root-coordinate) gradient *vectors*; vanishing of the *first moment* of the matrix $QBQ^\top$ is neither equivalent to nor obviously implies it. The inner product $\langle\xi(Q),\eta(Q)\rangle$ is a quadratic functional of $Q$, whose expectation involves *second* Weingarten moments of $O(n)$, not the first moment.

2. "Finite-$n$ form of asymptotic freeness" is a heuristic: freeness of independently rotated blocks is an $n\to\infty$ statement; finite-$n$ blocks are NOT free, so this cannot be cited as a finite-$n$ identity.

**What must be proved.** Once $\xi,\eta$ are given an explicit honest definition as elements of $H$ (see core-projection issue), one must compute $\mathbb E_Q\langle\xi(Q),\eta(Q)\rangle$ exactly (via second-order Weingarten calculus on $O(n)$) and show it equals $0$ — or replace (iii) by the correct non-orthogonal bookkeeping. As stated the orthogonality is asserted, not derived. Numerically $(\star)$ holds (verified n=2..6), so some correct version of the argument exists, but the current first-moment justification is a genuine logical gap.

This is distinct from q4-47/q4-52 (which concern the projection identity / inner product); this issue is specifically about the *orthogonality* hypothesis and its erroneous first-moment proof.
